title: Early Obesity Prediction Using Expert Knowledge and Machine Learning: Development and Comparative Evaluation of Obesity Risk Scores
content: Obesity develops through interacting familial, dietary, and lifestyle factors, highlighting the need for BMI-free screening tools to identify susceptibility before excess weight develops. This study developed an Obesity Risk Score (ORS) using 13 questionnaire predictors and compared three weighting strategies: consensus weights from five nutritionists (Expert ORS), Gradient Boosting-derived weights (GB ORS), and weights from three machine learning models (ML-3 ORS). Data-driven weights were derived from the current weight status of 2,084 records using nested cross-validation. All scores increased progressively across healthy weight, overweight, and obesity. The Expert ORS showed the strongest association with weight status (Spearman ρ = 0.458; AUC = 0.740 for obesity and 0.759 for overweight/obesity), classified 98.5% of individuals with obesity as High risk, and flagged 47.8% of non-overweight individuals as High risk. Although the scores ranked individuals similarly (ρ = 0.874–0.973), categorical agreement was limited (κ = 0.094–0.422). Twenty machine learning models reproduced the scores with high accuracy (XGBoost R² ≥ 0.997; best macro-F1 = 0.924–0.966). Family history was the most influential predictor. Expert-informed BMI-free scoring offers a transparent approach to assessing obesity susceptibility, requiring prospective and external validation before predictive use.
